lines: I know the smell of fear and smoke. You pushed both back from our doors.
There are clean cuts and ugly fights. That was ugly, but you helped finish it.
You kept the raid from reaching more kitchens than mine. I noticed.
The village smelled of smoke and fear. Then it smelled like survival.
You did hard work when hard work was needed. That matters.
I saw raiders turn from our doors because you were there.
No one wants that kind of fight, but someone had to answer it.
You helped keep families at their tables. That's worth saying aloud.
I moved the salt and cured meat away from the outer wall before the bell stopped ringing.
The livestock go into the inner pen now whenever a watch spots trouble.
We keep food in two cellars so one broken door cannot empty both.
A barrel of water sits beside the smoker for sparks, not thirst.
The heavy cutting table makes a fair barricade when the back gate fails.
I know which families need help reaching shelter before the square closes.
Every defender gets something to eat before taking the night watch.
The hooks come down during an alarm. Nobody needs sharp iron swinging overhead.
I keep bandages beside the knives because raids leave more than hunger behind.
One clear lane between the pens and the cellar matters more than another fence.
After an attack, I check the animals before panic makes them hurt themselves.
A village that can feed its watch can keep that watch awake.
